A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same work and have readable text, equations, figures and tables. All pages were inspected, including v2 Appendices A–C. The supplied v1 ends with references and contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original robot-policy simulation results on LIBERO and both SimplerEnv settings, plus decoding-strategy and temperature ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation results and adds Bridge task results, further ablations, a throughput–accuracy analysis and execution visualizations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain the backbone, action tokenization, bidirectional attention, masked cross-entropy, adaptive decoding and both remasking checks. Appendix C newly discloses Bridge-specific FiLM conditioning, but does not establish that this component was newly introduced relative to v1.

E1.justification: Table 3 adds the Put Eggplant in Basket task to the existing WidowX/Bridge evaluation. The four LIBERO suites, Google Robot tasks, training datasets and robot embodiments remain the same.

E2.justification: v2 adds GR00T-N1 to the WidowX comparison in Table 3; it previously appeared only in the other benchmark comparisons. Other comparator memberships are retained. Changes between pi0+FAST and pi0-FAST naming do not introduce a new baseline.

E3.justification: The reported Bridge action chunk size changes from 5 to 3 in Section 4.2. v2 also introduces a denoising-step sweep evaluated using throughput and LIBERO-Goal success. Existing LIBERO rollout counts, image resolution, backbone size and default 12 decoding steps remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends analysis of the decoder: Table 4 isolates secondary remasking, Figure 4 tests the denoising-step speed–accuracy trade-off, and Appendix B adds five execution sequences. v1 only ablated decoding strategy and temperature; its efficiency discussion used function-evaluation counts without the new throughput sweep.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. The new throughput–accuracy plot does not add uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 remain numerically unchanged, but Table 3 gains eggplant results and GR00T-N1 and revises Bridge values. The proposed method's spoon success changes from 37.5% to 29.2% and block-grasp success from 79.2% to 62.5%; its expanded overall average changes from 49.3% to 54.2% under the revised chunk size and task coverage. New results include 97.0% without secondary remasking versus the retained 97.4% full method, and approximately three chunks per second at 12 steps.

T1.justification: The substantive diffusion formalism, masked loss and decoding definitions are retained. The removed generic corruption equation duplicates retained mathematics, while top-k selection is restated in prose and the cosine schedule remains specified by name. No new theoretical result or proof appears.

C1.justification: The unified discrete-diffusion and adaptive-remasking contributions remain. v2 explicitly extends its framing to separate MLP action heads, while narrowing the conclusion's fewer-function-evaluations claim from continuous-diffusion and autoregressive baselines to autoregressive baselines alone.

C2.justification: v2 removes the explicit limitation concerning fixed-bin quantization and sub-bin precision loss, including the proposed continuous-space-loss direction. It adds a diminishing-returns interpretation of the step-count sweep to justify selecting 12 decoding steps.

D1.justification: v1 references an implementation appendix that is absent. v2 Appendix C supplies batch size 32, four A800 GPUs, benchmark-specific training budgets, best-checkpoint selection, Bridge FiLM conditioning and a numerical remasking threshold. These newly disclosed settings do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings. v2 also announces a future code location; release availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 distinguishes VPDD's discrete-diffusion policy learning from its claimed unified VLA and adds citations concerning parallel action decoding, action-specialized experts and InstructVLA. It removes Fast-dLLM, G3Flow and several tokenizer-background references, and reframes prior methods around unified token decoding versus separate action heads.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and several method explanations undergo substantial rewriting and compression. The separate autoregressive and diffusion VLA related-work subsections are merged, repeated explanations are reduced, and appendices for LLM disclosure, execution visualizations and implementation details are added.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the benchmark montage with robot illustrations and revised task imagery, expands the Bridge table, splits the combined ablation table into Tables 4–5, and adds the dual-axis Figure 4 and five execution storyboards. Several existing displays are also relocated.

improvement.justification: Appendix C and the new remasking and step-count analyses improve reproducibility and empirical support for decoder choices. The gain is limited by removal of the quantization limitation and new inconsistencies: Appendix C's decreasing threshold conflicts with Section 3.5's increasing threshold, and Figure 4's success markers do not fully support the claimed monotonic trend. The higher Bridge aggregate uses changed coverage and settings, so does not itself establish a performance improvement.
